scan_rule: An `unsafe` block is a boundary of kind `unsafe block` under the rule of the kernel safety-contract inventory (jit:7d44b71f), whose scanner this script runs on the working tree. A block is test code when it lies inside the braces of a module that a `#[cfg(test)]` attribute introduces. Its function is safe when the nearest preceding `fn` of the enclosing item's name is not an `unsafe fn`. Every safe function with a block outside test code is either an entry point of the inventory or cleared with a basis and a source claim.
use_rule: In every tracked Rust file outside receipt input snapshots and outside this record's own directory, whose witness example calls the pointers on purpose, a call is a line holding `.<field>)(` for a published pointer field of the inventory, doc comments included; a value use is `.<field>` in code text that no call parenthesis follows. Each file and field is assigned in the review with the entry points its uses reach and their counts.

sparse-row-index.title: Sparse row kernels: one index bound per stored non-zero
sparse-row-index.check: After one subtraction and one division per call, one comparison per non-zero of the row ahead of the kernel.
sparse-row-index.hoist: The scan runs once per row call and leaves the kernel's loops as they are: the kernel reads each index once per 16 output columns and once per remaining column. A check that sits beside a whole matrix needs the row loop inside the kernel crate.
sparse-row-index.hot_path: yes: one scan per sparse row of every product

ple-panel.title: PLE panel base kernels: window shape and inverse-table index
ple-panel.check: One checked product and one comparison per call for the window shape; a bounds-checked inverse-table read in place of the unchecked one.
ple-panel.granularity: per call, plus one comparison per pivot
ple-panel.hoist: The shape check stands ahead of the elimination. The index check stands at the pivot read, outside the Schur update loops; a check held wholly in the safe entry point scans every window entry.
ple-panel.hot_path: per pivot column, outside the row and lane loops

packed-lengths.title: Packed F_3, F_5 and F_7 batch kernels: equal lengths, a multiple of four
packed-lengths.check: One mask test and one length comparison per further slice, per call.
packed-lengths.hoist: The check stands ahead of the word loop. A caller that passes four words per call runs it once per vector iteration.
packed-lengths.hot_path: yes for the two F_3 kernels the single-word SIMD permanent calls once per Gray step; no tracked Rust file calls the other entry points

dense-shape-product.title: Dense kernels: shape products that wrap
dense-shape-product.check: `checked_mul` in place of each wrapping product the release assertions compare.
dense-shape-product.hoist: The comparisons exist; only their products change, ahead of every loop.
dense-shape-product.hot_path: no: once per matrix product, per row product or per demapped axis

dense-shape-product.reason: The assertions exist and compare with a wrapping product; `checked_mul` closes the gap once per call. The calling dispatchers size their operands from the same wrapping products, and no production caller can hold an `unsafe` block.

ple-panel.reason: The shape check is one product per panel and the index check one comparison per pivot, both outside the update loops; the two production callers meet both conditions by construction.

sparse-row-index.reason: The one production caller forwards column indices from a safe public hook and cannot hold an `unsafe` block, so an unchecked row kernel needs the row loop inside the kernel crate. The scan is one comparison per non-zero per row, on a hot path, and the M4RM tile wrappers set the precedent of an index check per call.

packed-lengths.reason: The check is a handful of comparisons per call. No tracked Rust file calls the F_5, F_7, F_3 mul and F_3 neg pointers. The F_3 add and sub pointers are called once per Gray step with four words, which puts the check beside one vector iteration; the crate publishes the unchecked form of those kernels as `unsafe fn` items.
